chapter: Uptown clubs and the Black Cat
title: Celebrities in the after-hours at the Yeah Man
summary: Lonnie Johnson, Jimmy Dorsey, June Clark and others dropped in, and Greene and Simmons were awestruck country boys.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Because that -- the Yeah Man Club was the first time I heard time I heard Lonnie Johnson.
Lonnie Johnson came in there one night, and really upset things. (laugh).

Yeah. He was singing this thing -- "Tomorrow Night" or something like that, you know. And, that's where I first heard [ ] -- I heard all of the celebrities in that club. It was a big thing for me, you know.
What sort of club was The Yeah Man?
It was like -- well, they had [boozes] [booths] and a couple of singers, you know.
They had a singer named Detroit Red.
And, the -- Marjorie [ ] She was a ballad singer, I guess.
And Detroit Red was singing there like a suggestive singer.
Yeah. So, like when you heard Lonnie Johnson, would they bring a star in? Would a star come in or how did you hear
No, no, no. Well, they -- the star -- they used to come in -- it was like an after-hour.
People used to come up from downtown.
And, all over -- like I saw the two brothers -- musicians -- the two band leaders --
Jimmy used to come in there at the Yeah Man, and like, all the celebrities used to come in there.
I saw June Clark came in -- used to come in there. That's when June was -- used to be a real good trumpet player.
He had quite a good reputation.
Yeah. Yeah. He was a good --
What happened to him? Did his chops go?
I don't know what happened to June But, during that period he was, you know --
Oh, you must have -- it must have been very thrilling for you?
Every time the door would open, you know, we would -- for both of us -- Lennie and myself, you know, because we were two country boys.
And, you know, all of a sudden these big stars are coming in.
